text:
B: Hello, there we go. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, hello. I can hear you. I'm Rasa.
B: Darren. Nice to meet you. Where are you calling from, then?
A: Leyton, East London. And you?
B: Kesgrave, just outside Ipswich. Suffolk.
A: Ah, okay. I don't know it, sorry. I know Ipswich only from the train board.
B: Ha, that's most people, to be fair. It's alright, it's quiet. So what do you do, Rasa?
A: I work in a bakery in Walthamstow. Part-time, Saturday morning and one day in the week. Saturday is crazy, queue out the door from eight o'clock.
B: I bet. What, all the sausage rolls?
A: Sausage rolls, yeah, and the bread. Everybody wants sourdough now. I bring home what is left at the end, so we never buy bread, that's good. And you? I guessed from your photo maybe builder or plumber.
B: Not far off. Gas engineer. Boilers, mainly. Installs, servicing, breakdowns. Got me own business, one van, been doing it about fourteen years.
A: Oh, really? Then I need you. My boiler, every winter it stops. The pressure goes down, and the landlord takes like two weeks to send someone.
B: Yeah, that's a classic, that. Pressure dropping, you've probably got a little leak somewhere or the expansion vessel's gone. Landlord's probably just getting the cheapest bloke round to top it up, you know.
A: Yes! Exactly. The man comes, he does something for five minutes and goes. And then three weeks later, again.
B: Sounds about right. It's mad busy in the winter anyway. Everyone's boiler packs up the first cold week. I was doing twelve-hour days in January.
A: Twelve hours, every day? You must be knackered.
B: Yeah, the knees aren't what they were, to be fair. I'm hoping to take on an apprentice in a year or two, so I can do more of the quoting and less lying on kitchen floors.
A: That makes sense. My husband is electrician, he says same thing about his back.
B: Oh, is he? Self-employed?
A: No, he works for a company, maintenance for buildings. This week he is in Stratford on a job. He likes it, regular money, you know.
B: Yeah, there's a lot to be said for that. Being your own boss sounds good till the van breaks down. Mine's been playing up, sensor fault, had it in the garage last week. Are you from London originally?
A: No, I'm from Lithuania, from Šiauliai. I came in 2006. So, nearly twenty years now.
B: Twenty years, blimey. Do you get back much?
A: Every summer. Two, three weeks with my mum and my sister. We fly from Stansted, Ryanair. My daughter, she is twelve, she loves it there because grandma spoils her.
B: Course she does. Mine were the same with my mum. We usually do Spain or Turkey, all-inclusive, pool, bit of sun. Did Florida once with the kids, that was something.
A: Florida, wow. That's expensive, no?
B: Erm, yeah, you don't want to know. Worth it, though. Lithuania, that's basketball, isn't it? I remember something about that.
A: Yes! Basketball is like religion there. I don't really follow, but when Lithuania plays in big tournament, my husband watches and I have to watch too. That's it, really.
B: Ha, same as me with Ipswich and my wife. She just sits there on her phone.
A: Yeah, same. I make dinner and I hear him shouting from the other room.
B: Sounds like ours on a Saturday. Right, I reckon we're nearly out of time.
A: Yeah, it's fast. Nice to talk to you, Darren.
B: You too, Rasa. Get your landlord to sort that vessel out.
